Welcome to a journey that reaches far beyond the familiar stories of World War Two—a journey into the shadows where history, memory, and secrecy collide.
What if the greatest mysteries of the past weren’t locked away on distant battlefields, but hidden in the choices, cover-ups, and whispered secrets that continue to shape the world we know today?
In Who Has Buried the Dead?: From Stalin to Putin … The last great secret of World War Two, K.G.E. Konkel invites us to pull back the curtain on some of the most enduring enigmas of Russia’s twentieth-century history.
Together, we’ll explore how the aftermath of war became a battleground for truth and power, where the manipulation of memory and the careful erasing of evidence set the stage for decades of political intrigue.
Imagine stepping into a world where the fate of the dead—both in spirit and in fact—stands as a haunting symbol for all the unanswered questions that linger in Russia’s past and present.
As we move forward, get ready to uncover the personal bravery it takes to challenge the official story, and just what’s at stake when history is rewritten, or sometimes, simply forgotten.
Let’s explore the hidden corridors of the Kremlin, the echoes of Stalin’s regime, and the secrets that still shape modern Russia—because understanding these buried truths could change the way we see the world, and ourselves.
